name: Austin
title: Family holidays in Austin
intro: Spring-fed pools, barbecue and a million bats at sunset. Here's what Austin is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Spring and autumn are perfect, with warm days and wildflowers in April. July and August are very hot, so plan pool time and indoor afternoons. Hotel prices jump during big events like SXSW in March and the Formula 1 race in autumn.

things.name: Barton Springs Pool
things.blurb: A huge natural pool fed by springs that stays around 20°C all year.

things.name: Congress Avenue Bridge bats
things.blurb: Up to 1.5 million bats fly out at dusk, March to October.

things.name: Thinkery
things.blurb: A hands-on children's museum for under-11s.

things.name: Zilker Park
things.blurb: Wide lawns, a miniature train and kayaks on Lady Bird Lake.

things.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
things.blurb: Texas history with a shipwreck and an IMAX cinema.

things.name: Hamilton Pool
things.blurb: A swimming hole under a collapsed cave. Book well ahead.

faqs.question: Is Austin good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for families who like the outdoors and good food. It's relaxed and friendly, though you'll want a car to get around.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four to six nights, or pair it with San Antonio, about 90 minutes away, for a Texas road trip.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Is there a direct flight from the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes, British Airways flies direct from London Heathrow, so it's easier than many US cities to reach.
